study_material.title: Series (Number and Letter) - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Series questions ask for the next term or the odd one out. The generating rules are limited: constant difference, changing difference, multiplication, squares/cubes, primes, Fibonacci, and alternating/mixed patterns. Test them in that order.
learning_objectives: Identify arithmetic, geometric and second-difference patterns
Recognise square, cube, prime and Fibonacci series
Solve letter series with position arithmetic
Spot the wrong term in a corrupted series

concepts.heading: 1. Difference Patterns
concepts.body: Compute successive differences first. Constant difference = arithmetic (5, 9, 13...). Differences growing by a constant = quadratic pattern (2, 6, 12, 20 with differences 4, 6, 8 - next is 30). If first differences look messy, try second differences.

concepts.heading: 2. Ratio Patterns
concepts.body: If each term divides the next evenly, it is geometric: 3, 6, 12, 24 doubles. Mixed rules like 'x2 + 1' also appear: 3, 7, 15, 31. Test the ratio when differences fail.

concepts.heading: 3. Special Number Families
concepts.body: Squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25; cubes 1, 8, 27, 64, 125; primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13; Fibonacci 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 (each term = sum of previous two); n^2+1, n^2-1 variants like 2, 5, 10, 17, 26.

concepts.heading: 4. Letter Series
concepts.body: Convert letters to positions. A, C, F, J, O has gaps 2, 3, 4, 5 - next gap 6 gives U. Alternating series interleave two independent patterns - separate the odd and even positions before hunting a rule.

formulas: Letter position arithmetic with A=1 ... Z=26
shortcut_methods: Check differences, then ratios, then special families - in that order
For odd-one-out, find the rule the majority obeys
Interleaved series: split alternate terms into two rows
common_mistakes: Forcing an arithmetic rule onto a geometric series
Stopping at the first rule that fits only two terms
study_material.summary: Differences, ratios, special families, interleaving - four checks crack almost every series.
quick_revision_notes: Split alternating series into two sub-series

solved_examples.question: Find the next term: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Differences are 4, 6, 8, 10 - next difference 12 gives 42. (Terms are n(n+1).)

solved_examples.question: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?

practice_questions.question: Next letter: Z, X, U, Q, ?
Next term: 1, 10, 3, 20, 5, 30, ?
practice_questions.explanation: Two interleaved series: 1,3,5,7 and 10,20,30. The 7th term belongs to the odd series: 7.

practice_questions.question: Find the wrong term: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 36, 50
practice_questions.explanation: Pattern n^2+1 gives 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50 - the 36 should be 37.

topic_test.title: Series - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Check differences first, then ratios, then special families.

questions.question: Next letter: B, D, F, H, ?
Next letter pair: AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.explanation: First letters ascend, second letters descend (opposite pairs).

questions.question: Find the wrong term: 3, 10, 27, 4, 16, 64, 5, 25, 125
questions.explanation: Triplets are n, n^2, n^3: 3, 9, 27 - the 10 should be 9.
